sections.title: Hollywood Directors (PD)
sections.description:
What does a film director do, anyway? There is no one answer. This course is a deep dive into the careers of seven or eight different film directors (the directors we look at change from semester to semester). We will consider their overall vision, their stylistic choices, and how they work as part of a collaborative team (actors, cinematographers, etc).
We will look at how they negotiate(d) the larger context in which they work(ed): industry, politics, and social environment. We will examine films from early Hollywood history, through the golden age of the studio system, the New Hollywood of the late 1960s and 1970s, the influence of independent film in the 1990s, and the changes brought by digital film, online distribution and streaming, and interaction with new media platforms. Hollywood has always been a global industry, and we will consider the diverse, global range of directors who have come to Hollywood to tell stories.
Directors studied might include: Dorothy Arzner, Billy Wilder, Spike Lee, Steven Spielberg, Guillermo Del Toro, Greta Gerwig, Charles Chaplin, Preston Sturges, Sofia Coppola, Joan Micklin Silver, Todd Haynes, Jodie Foster, Chloé Zhao, Stanley Kubrick, and John Woo, among many others. We will also hear from working directors over Zoom and possibly in person. (Again, the directors studied vary each time the course is offered.)
There is also a practical production component to the class. Students will engage in in-class exercises and homework to hone their own directing skills.
This is an SNF Paideia-designated course and is open to all Penn students, not just Paideia fellows.
